worker_affinity: InkFuse worker 0 uses logical CPU 0; Roc entire process taskset CPU 0
inkfuse_compiler: Clang 14, -O3 -march=native; interpreter linked with runtime bitcode using LTO
roc_compiler: LLVM 19.1.7 through Inkwell 0.7.1; Rust 1.95.0; existing experiment code unchanged
baseline_provenance: 300 upstream files hashed; only CMakeLists.txt and QueryExecutor.cpp/.h differ. Differences add benchmark target and wait-for-compilation helper. All execution, codegen, suboperator and runtime implementations match upstream. Original runtime bitcode restored with inkfuse_install_runtime before running.
timing: Resident input. Input creation/loading, fragment startup, physical-plan construction and QueryControlBlock creation excluded.
prepare_ms: construct StepwiseExecutor, prepareQuery, and for full compilation join all compiler jobs. This recompiles each query and does not imply a query cache exists.

elapsed_ms: runQuery and executor destruction; includes runtime state initialization, pipeline scheduling and runtime tasks. Interpreted fragment runner setup is deferred by upstream to runQuery and is therefore included in elapsed_ms.
Zero compile means no query-specific compilation after fragment prewarm. InkFuse fragment startup measured about 3.5 seconds and is excluded from query timings.
Warmup attaches output stream for correctness validation; timed runs materialize chunks and count rows but do not print results.

TPC-H initial run retained; confirmation is reported because a separate harness was built while the initial run was in progress. Confirmation, chain run and Roc diagnostic runs had no concurrent benchmark/build started by this task.
TPC-H: 1 validation warmup per mode/query, 7 measured samples, rotated mode order. Two process runs; confirmation is primary. Single-thread only.
Synthetic: 4,000,000 signed Int64, non-NULL values (i % 1000) - 500, chain of x + 1 + ... + N, N in 0/1/16/64. 1 all-row validation warmup per mode/depth and 15 timed samples, alternating modes.

Roc diagnostic: 3 independent processes per mode/nullability, 20 samples each, report median of per-process medians. Existing arithmetic_chain workload, all-row validation and duplicate/missing-ID checks retained. Nonnullable changes input schema, expression nullability and data; overflow checks remain.
comparability_limits: TPC-H uses upstream hand-built relational plans and simplified schema; this is not an official TPC-H result. Q13 excluded because previous independent validation found upstream wrong results. This run validates mode-to-mode numeric output agreement, not an independent SQL implementation.
InkFuse arithmetic uses unchecked C signed addition and no NULL values. Roc preserves checked overflow; its original data has one NULL in 17 rows.

InkFuse Print materializes and reuses 512-row output buffers and retains no full result. Roc collects Arrow RecordBatches including ID plus result and retains output until execution ends. Cross-engine absolute times are not equivalent-work comparisons.
Roc zero execution window is 1024 rows inside 8192-row Arrow batches, stores intermediate variables in u64 arrays (including Boolean flags). InkFuse uses typed 512-row columns.
Roc nullable/nonnullable ablation measures NULL handling plus changes enabled by non-null data/schema; it does not isolate only the And kernels.

Machine powersave governor and incidental external activity can alter clock speed. Current paired Roc absolute timings differ from the previous experiment; do not mix them as a controlled before/after.
correctness: All 16 TPC-H query/run mode comparisons matched (floating relative tolerance 1e-8, absolute 1e-7). All eight InkFuse chain mode/depth warmups independently validated every one of 4M values. Roc warmups use existing independent value/NULL/ID checks.
